1.why: Density measures how much mass is packed into a given volume.

wrong.d: Speed is distance divided by time.

2.why: V stands for volume in the density equation.

wrong.b: Velocity is speed in a direction.

3.why: Adding soot and ash increases the mass of particles in the same air volume, raising density.

wrong.a: Soot adds particles, not removes air.
wrong.b: Mass increases when smoke is added.
wrong.d: Smoke does not turn air into water.

_quiz_pool.question: What does density measure?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Density is mass divided by volume.

_quiz_pool.question: What is the unit of density in SI?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Density is measured in kilograms per cubic metre.

_quiz_pool.question: If you add heavy smoke to air, what happens to its density?
_quiz_pool.explanation: More mass in the same volume increases density.

_quiz_pool.question: What does m stand for in ρ = m ÷ V?
What does V stand for in ρ = m ÷ V?
Why is smoke haze harmful?
options: It carries tiny particles that affect breathing
It cools the ground too much

_quiz_pool.question: Which gas or particle is added by forest fires?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Fires release ash, soot, and smoke particles.

_quiz_pool.question: What does 1 kg/m³ mean?
_quiz_pool.explanation: It means one kilogram of mass in every cubic metre of space.

_quiz_pool.question: Where were many hotspots found during forest fires?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Reports show many hotspots were in corporate working areas.

_quiz_pool.question: What tool helps monitor air quality and smoke from space?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Satellites monitor smoke and air composition worldwide.

cover.subtitle: Forest fires send thousands of hotspots and thick smoke across Indonesia. Discover what density tells us about smoke particles in the air.

cover.fun_fact: Between January and September 2026, Indonesia recorded 30,927 hotspots across forests and land [1].
story.title: Fires, smoke and hazy skies
story.lead: Between January and September 2026, thousands of hotspots flared up across Indonesia's forests and land [1]. Thick smoke filled the air, reducing visibility and harming people and wildlife [2].

story.body_1: Forest and land fires, known as karhutla, happen during dry spells and damage ecosystems [1]. Reports show that half of all hotspots were inside working areas of palm oil and forestry corporations [1]. West Kalimantan and Central Kalimantan recorded the highest numbers [1].
story.body_2: Thick smoke carries tiny ash and soot particles that spread across regions and even cross borders [1]. Breathing smoky air harms health, especially for children and wildlife struggling with habitat loss and respiratory stress [2].
timeline.1.text: Forests and peatlands dry out, becoming very easy to ignite.
timeline.2.text: Hotspots spread across corporate concessions and vulnerable lands [1].
timeline.3.text: Fires release fine particles, and smoke spreads through the air [3].
physics.title: Mass, volume and density
physics.body_1: When forest fires burn, they release massive amounts of smoke, ash, and gases into the atmosphere. To understand how concentrated this smoke is, physicists use density: how much mass is packed into a given volume.
physics.body_2: Density is mass divided by volume. If you take a specific volume of air, adding soot and ash increases its mass, making the air denser with harmful particles.
physics.assumptions: We assume smoke particles mix evenly through the tested air volume.
example.step_1: m = 0.015 kg soot, V = 50 m³ air

physics.tip: More mass in the same volume means higher density. Thick smoke means more soot particles packed into every cubic metre of air!
